name: KYC update demanded through a link or inbound call
description: A KYC update is demanded via a link or an inbound call, under time pressure or a suspension threat. Legitimate institutions do reference KYC, so the pretext alone carries no weight — the combination with pressure and an off-channel action does.

source_references.quote: Bank Account / Payment Wallet / SIM / Gas / Electricity / KYC update, impersonation as Government official, sextortion

explanation.plain: You have been asked to complete a KYC update through a link or a call you did not initiate, with a deadline attached. Banks do ask for KYC, but they do not force it through a link under threat of your account being blocked.
explanation.technical: KYC_PRETEXT with an off-channel action and a pressure indicator, spanning three evidence classes. Severity is capped at MEDIUM: the 'banks never ask via link or call' phrasing traces only to a commercial source whose page no longer resolves (D5).
verification_steps: Open your bank's own app, or visit a branch. A genuine KYC requirement will be visible there.
Do not use any number or link from the message itself.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: Only the Chakshu category listing is verified — it confirms KYC fraud is a recognised reporting category, not the specific 'never via link' guidance this rule leans on. Severity is capped accordingly until an official equivalent is retrieved (G-04).
